The plan adds a 202 response on POST /uploads and new 409 scan_pending and 410 file_infected responses on GET /files/{id}, but scope.files lists neither api/openapi.yaml nor docs/api.md. Convention 5 says: "A new HTTP route, response field or status code updates `api/openapi.yaml` (the source of truth) and `docs/api.md` (the human companion) in the same change." Resolve by adding both files to scope as modify and documenting the new status codes and error codes. Also note that the upload response changes from its current success shape to 202 with a file id.

Migration 0052 defaults scan_status to pending for every row, including files uploaded before this change. No scan job is ever enqueued for those rows, so GET /files/{id} would return 409 scan_pending for all pre-existing files indefinitely. That breaks downloads of existing attachments, and it also misses the issue's requirement that every file be scanned before download. The plan needs a backfill that enqueues scans for existing rows (or a documented migration of them), with a test, and the rollback section should state the consequence.

The plan does not say how a scan job is lost or fails. It does not state whether ScanQueue is durable or in-process. A process restart, a full queue, an enqueue failure after the file row is stored as pending, a clamd outage or timeout, or a file over clamd's stream size limit would all leave the file stuck in scan_pending forever. There is no retry, no scan-error state, and no recovery sweep of pending rows. It fails closed, which is good, but it is not operable. The plan should define the queue durability, the handling of enqueue failure on POST /uploads, and worker retry or error behaviour, and add tests for these paths.

(3) The test strategy promises a worker test with a fake clamd and an upload-returns-202 test, but the only test file in scope is internal/api/files_test.go. No internal/scan/*_test.go or uploads test is listed. This review is diff-only, so these may live in files not shown, but the plan should list every file it touches. Step 1 adds scan_status to the existing files table with a default of pending, and the plan has no backfill. That breaks downloads of all existing attachments and contradicts ac-download-clean-200 for them. Resolving it needs either a migration that marks existing rows clean (or a rescan), or a one-off enqueue of existing rows, plus a test for the pre-existing-file case.

Files can get stuck in pending with no recovery path. Step 3 only sets clean or infected, so a clamd error, timeout or unreachable daemon leaves the row pending forever. The ScanQueue's durability is also unspecified: if it is in-memory, a restart loses queued jobs, and if the enqueue in step 2 fails after the row is stored, the handler still returns 202. This affects ac-upload-enqueues-scan and ac-download-pending-409. Resolving it needs a defined failure and retry policy (a retry, a scan_failed or error state, or a re-enqueue sweep of pending rows on startup), and a specified handler response when the enqueue fails. The policy should fail closed so unscanned files are never served.
